newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies sharply up on cash market gains.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies sharply up on cash market gains.

text.p: CME hog futures were sharply higher at midsession on strength from higher-than-expected cash hog markets, and pork bellies were higher on commercial buying, CME floor traders said.
Initial cash hog calls were mostly steady, but hogs in key Midwestern trade sold $0.50 to as much as $1.50 per cwt higher early Friday, according to USDA data.
"Sharply higher cash hogs mean sharply higher futures," one floor trader said.
Forecasts for good harvest weather throughout the Midwest were limiting numbers of slaughter hogs, traders said.
Packers Trading was a heavy buyer this morning, and commodity funds were covering short positions, floor sources said.
The pace of gains in hog futures accelerated when buy-stop orders were triggered as December hogs surpassed Thursday's high of 55.050 cents, floor traders said.
Additional short covering was expected if December hogs move through the 40-day moving average near 55.67 cents per lb, and February pushes through 75.87 cent, one technical trader said.
Heavy buying by a trader with ties to the cash market pushed pork bellies sharply higher in early trade, sources said.
Other supportive factors in bellies included expectations that the weekly hog slaughter will be three to six percent below year-ago levels, traders and analysts said.

At 1050 CST, December live hogs were up 1.15 cent at 55.550 cents per lb and February was up 1.475 at 75.625 cent. Other months were trading up 0.275 to 1.125 cent. February pork bellies were up 1.85 cent at 70.15 cents a lb, with other months up 0.90 to 1.72 cent.
